result: The six-edge list is exactly correct for EVERY n>=26, with no additional proviso: the largest positive difference between the eight old tail residues is 14 and the largest forbidden old-head difference is 11, so n>=26>14+11 implies n−d>11 for each positive old-tail difference d. Therefore no wrap gap can equal a forbidden magnitude. The six edges are the ordinary positive-difference matches.
direct_check: Owner eval kernel enumerated all six edges at n=26,27,28,29,30,31,32. The general statement follows from the maximum-sum inequality, not finite extrapolation.
scope: This supersedes only the earlier overly cautious threshold caveat. The disjointness graph itself remains a necessary same-D observation, not a complete code or accepted no-go.
